BBQ Chicken Thighs with Corn and Sweet Potato [american-bbq-chicken-traybake] for 6 servings.

Per serving: 650 kcal, protein 48 g, carbs 81 g, fat 17 g. Allergens: mustard, sulphites.

Ingredients:
- 1200 g chicken thighs
- 1050 g sweet potatoes
- 900 g sweetcorn
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2.25 tsp salt
- 1.5 tsp black pepper
- 1.5 tsp paprika
- 1.5 tsp garlic powder
- 180 ml ketchup
- 3 tbsp brown sugar
- 1.5 tbsp cider vinegar
- 1.5 tsp mustard
- 3 tbsp water

Steps:
1. Heat the oven to 220°C. Line a large baking tray with baking paper if you have it.
2. Cut the sweet potatoes into bite-sized chunks. Toss them with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Spread them on the tray and roast for 15 minutes.
3. Meanwhile, mix the ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar, mustard, water, paprika, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt in a bowl to make the barbecue sauce.
4. Pat the chicken thighs dry, season with the remaining salt and pepper, then toss with the barbecue sauce until well coated.
5. Remove the tray from the oven, add the sweetcorn and chicken thighs, and turn the sweet potatoes. Drizzle the sweetcorn with the remaining olive oil.
6. Return to the oven and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, the juices run clear, and the sweet potatoes are browned at the edges.
7. If you want a stickier glaze, brush the chicken with any extra sauce and roast for 3 to 5 minutes more. Serve the chicken with the roasted sweet potato and sweetcorn.

Baking soda and baking powder are both leaveners, but they work differently:

- **Baking soda** = pure **sodium bicarbonate**. It needs an **acid** in the batter or dough to react, like buttermilk, yogurt, lemon juice, vinegar, brown sugar, or cocoa. It makes bubbles right away, so you usually bake soon after mixing.
- **Baking powder** = **baking soda + an acid already built in** (plus starch). It only needs **moisture** to start working, so it’s more self-contained.

Quick rule:
- Use **baking soda** when the recipe already has acidic ingredients.
- Use **baking powder** when it doesn’t.

A couple of practical notes:
- Too much **baking soda** can taste soapy or metallic.
- Some baking powders are **double-acting**, meaning they react once when mixed and again in the oven.

Chocolate Cake

Ingredients for 8 servings:
- 250 g plain flour
- 200 g sugar
- 60 g cocoa powder
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 pinch salt
- 2 eggs
- 240 ml milk
- 120 ml vegetable oil
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 240 ml hot water
- 115 g butter
- 300 g icing sugar
- 30 g cocoa powder
- 3 tbsp milk

Method:
- Heat the oven to 180 C and grease and line two 20 cm cake tins.
- In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
- Add the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla, then mix until smooth.
- Stir in the hot water carefully; the batter will be thin.
- Divide the batter between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
- Let the cakes cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.
- To make the frosting, beat the butter until smooth, then mix in the icing sugar, cocoa powder and milk until fluffy.
- Spread frosting between the layers and over the top of the cooled cake.

Note: the draft contains gluten, eggs, and milk.

Classic Beef Lasagne

Summary: A rich, comforting beef lasagne with a simple tomato meat sauce, creamy béchamel, and plenty of cheese. It bakes into layered, hearty slices that are perfect for dinner.

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion
- 3 garlic cloves
- 500 g beef mince
- 700 ml tomato passata
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried basil
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 50 g butter
- 50 g plain flour
- 600 ml milk
- 1 pinch nutmeg
- 12 lasagne sheets
- 200 g mozzarella
- 50 g parmesan

Method:
- Heat the oven to 180°C. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
- Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
- Add the beef mince and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
- Stir in the tomato paste, passata, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thickened.
- For the béchamel, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
- Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth, then cook until thick and creamy. Season with nutmeg, a little salt, and pepper.
- Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a baking dish. Add a layer of lasagne sheets, then meat sauce, then béchamel. Repeat, finishing with béchamel.
- Top with mozzarella and parmesan.
- Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 to 15 minutes before slicing and serving.

**Banana Bread**
- 3 ripe bananas
- 250 g plain flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 pinch salt
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 75 g butter
- 150 g brown sugar
- 2 eggs
- 60 ml milk
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

**Method**
- Preheat the oven to 175°C and grease or line a loaf pan.
- Mash the bananas in a large bowl.
- In another bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
- In a separate bowl, cream the butter and brown sugar until combined, then beat in the eggs, milk, and vanilla.
- Stir the banana mash into the wet ingredients.
- Fold in the dry ingredients just until no dry streaks remain.
- Pour the batter into the loaf pan and bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
- Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely before slicing.
